notes: Summary: Mid-market SaaS company building a multi-tenant agent platform for customer support and routing. Primary objective is to ship a hosted-based POC to validate two things: (1) streaming stability for user-facing chat with tool calling (live tool invocations, webhooks) and (2) per-tenant quotas and rate limiting accuracy under noisy neighbors. They are latency-sensitive: quoted target is p95 end-to-end < 250ms for assistant text generation (excluding network), < 500ms for tool-call roundtrips; willing to accept slightly higher p99 during cold starts but want mitigation strategies (prefetching, KV caching).
detailed_requirements:
- Workloads: real-time streaming chat for agents + automated assistant workflows; heavy use of tool calling (external APIs, DB lookups) and structured function outputs.
- Scalability: ~1k active tenants initially, plans to double in 12 months. Concurrent sessions per tenant vary; testing will simulate up to 12k concurrent open streams.
- Quotas: need per-tenant rate limits (RPS + token caps), dynamic quota adjustments by account, usage-based throttling with informative 429 payloads.
- SLOs: streaming stability (no more than 1% dropped streams under 95th percentile load), p95 token latency <250ms for gen models, deterministic fallback to smaller model if latency budget exceeded.
- Security/compliance: SSO (SAML), SOC2 alignment, audit logs for tokens & tool-calls, optional KMS integration for customer-managed keys.
- Data residency: prefer NA initially; possible EU region for enterprise accounts.
- Observability: token-level cost breakdown, per-tenant latency dashboards, tracing for tool calls.
- Pricing sensitivity: mid-market procurement; lean toward hosted for dev/POC but need committed pricing for Dedicated if capacity required.
quote_from_product_lead: "We need streaming that doesn't glitch on agent handoffs — if a user triggers a tool call, the UI must stay live while the function runs. Also, per-tenant throttles can't be global blunt instruments; they must be fine-grained."
poc_plan: 1) Week 1: baseline smoke tests on Hosted API (streaming + tool calling) using realistic traffic generator (simulate 1k tenants). 2) Week 2: stress run (12k concurrent streams), verify per-tenant quotas and graceful degradation (fallback model, queued requests). Deliverable: pass/fail report and perf dashboard. If pass -> present Dedicated TCO and reserved capacity options.
poc_success_criteria:
- No more than 1% dropped streams during stress run.
- Per-tenant quotas enforced correctly (sampled tenants show RPS and token caps applied).
- p95 generation latency <250ms for baseline model under typical load.
- Tool-calls are traceable end-to-end in observability and errors surface with clear diagnostics.
pricing_notes: Interested in committed Dedicated pricing if POC shows predictable gains vs hosted; budget range discussed: $75k-$250k ARR. Ask: show Dedicated latency SLOs and burst policy (can we keep some hosted burst window?).
